task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: how to define 'PNR fail' as a trigger
how to define 'lift' of PULL_UP as a counter
what is the appropriate unit of analysis (team, season, series, game)
how to achieve sufficient sample size per unit for the proportion and median thresholds
how to control for confounding variables (game situation, opponent, team strength)
how to avoid lookahead bias in defining failure
how robust are play-type labels, especially for PULL_UP inferred from play-by-play

historical_evidence.finding: Pre-game PT PPP ranking correlates with actual efficiency ranking in held-out games. Median rho +0.539; 90.8% positive lift. Caveat: top-3 lift partly reflects league-wide high-efficiency PTs (CUT, PUTBACK, TRANSITION).
Raw R1 TOV-force channel lifts shrink ~50%+ after adversary re-route and counter; net lift is model-implied, not observed in games; many R3 cells used n<10 surrogates.
Team-PT lifts are small (e.g., ORL PNR +1.2pp); player-channel lifts large on small n (n_def=17, n_off=54); primary defender attribution includes helpers; no holdout or game-outcome check.
Playoff defenses reduce DRIVE PPP and share; PULL_UP PPP +0.341, share -7.6pp relative to RS; PNR share +12.1pp; no inferential test, tagging differences possible.
Giannis forced PULL_UP PPP 0.848, -0.540 gap vs preferred DRIVE (largest gap); n>=30 for cited lineup cells.
Rank-1 suppressor varies across players; Jokic after opp POST_UP PPP 1.1271 (-0.0675, SE +/-0.0500); OTHER artifact flagged in doc; no multiple-comparison control.

failed_approaches.what_failed: using top-3 play-type lift as evidence of counter effectiveness without adjusting for base-rate efficiency of high-efficiency play types
failed_approaches.why: lift partly driven by league-wide high-efficiency PTs; 10.5% of rows have rho<0 (C_artifact)

failed_approaches.what_failed: estimating surviving counter lift on tiny samples with model-implied net values
failed_approaches.why: cells with n<10, net lift model-implied not observed, shrinkage >50% (E_unclear)

failed_approaches.what_failed: decomposing player-channel lifts from limited defensive possessions
failed_approaches.why: insufficient exposure (n 15-54), helper contamination, no holdout (A_unanswerable, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY)

evidence_establishes: Lift metrics can be computed from play-type possessions and correlate with efficiency rankings (SF-[prior work]).
Small-n lifts can be large and misleading; they shrink substantially under adversarial checks (SF-[prior work], SF-[prior work]).
PULL_UP can appear as a forced alternative when a star's preferred play type is suppressed (SF-[prior work]).
Playoff vs regular-season context changes PULL_UP efficiency and share patterns (SF-[prior work]).
No prior study directly tested the league-wide PULL_UP counter after PNR failure.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether PULL_UP after PNR failure yields positive lift in >=70% of units with median lift >2pp.
The correct unit of analysis, definition of 'PNR fail', baseline for lift, or robustness to confounding in this specific counter hypothesis.
own_inferences: The hypothesis posits a directional, quantitative threshold (70% positive lift, median >2pp) that requires precise estimation of a proportion and a median across many units, demanding careful power analysis.

'PNR fail' must be defined temporally (e.g., within-game H1 suppression trigger, rolling efficiency window) to avoid lookahead bias, but the trigger definition itself may be unstable in small samples.

PULL_UP as a play type is often a low-efficiency option (many are contested mid-range shots); any observed lift could be regression to the mean if the baseline PULL_UP efficiency is unusually low when PNR fails.
Confounding by game situation (score, clock, opponent adjustments) and team heterogeneity will be difficult to fully control without detailed stratification, reducing usable sample.

The play-type classifier's reliability for PULL_UP (often inferred from action type and sub-type) may introduce measurement error, especially in noisy play-by-play data, which can bias lift estimates.
uncertainties: The exact operational definition of 'PNR fail' and 'lift' as intended by the researcher.
Whether the derived play-type possession records reliably distinguish PULL_UP from other off-dribble jumpers (e.g., step-backs, floaters).
The number of qualifying 'units' (e.g., team-seasons) that will have sufficient PULL_UP possessions after PNR failure to estimate individual-unit lift with adequate precision.
The degree to which defensive strategies that force PULL_UP also affect the efficiency of other play types, potentially creating correlated errors across units.
Stability of the counter effect across seasons and coaching changes (non-stationarity).

historical_effect.explanation: No prior study directly answered the research question. The historical evidence confirms that lift measurement on small samples is unreliable and that apparent lifts can be artifacts of base-rate effects or model construction, but these insights reinforce pre-existing concerns rather than changing the decision.

blocking_constraints.text: The requirement of >=70% positive lift across units with median>2pp demands a large number of independent units with enough possessions each; it is unclear whether the available data provides sufficient power after applying the necessary temporal and contextual filters.

PULL_UP possessions following a PNR failure may be rare, especially if 'failure' is defined stringently (e.g., only sharp within-game suppression triggers). Sparse events per unit inflate variance and undermine unit-level lift estimates.
Game situation (score margin, period, opponent defensive strength, rest days) and team-specific baseline PULL_UP efficiency are likely confounded with whether PNR fails and the observed lift.
Defining 'PNR fail' from the same game's outcomes (e.g., low PNR PPP) can create circularity if the lift measurement window overlaps with the failure window, introducing selection bias.

PULL_UP classification from play-by-play relies on action-type heuristics that may mislabel possessions, particularly when differentiating between pull-ups and other off-dribble shots, attenuating or inflating lift.

prior_work.summary: Retrieved studies address aspects of lift measurement, small-sample adversarial lift shrinkage, forced PULL_UP as a suppression outcome, and playoff contextual changes, but none directly test the PNR failure to PULL_UP counter hypothesis.

risks.text: High risk that the number of units with adequate PULL_UP-after-PNR-failure possessions is too small to reliably estimate unit-level lift and test the 70% proportion and median 2pp thresholds.
Per-unit counter events may be sparse, leading to wide confidence intervals and inflated false-positive rates for unit-level positive lift.
Unmeasured confounders (opponent defensive scheme, game script, initiator quality) could drive both the PNR failure signal and PULL_UP efficiency.
If 'PNR fail' is defined from the same possessions used to measure lift, the design risks selection bias and artificial lift.
Play-type classification for PULL_UP may not be precise enough to avoid systematic measurement error in the lift estimate.
Conditioning on PNR failure could select periods of unusually low PNR efficiency, making PULL_UP lift partly a regression-to-the-mean artifact.
Testing a proportion of positive-lift units across many units without multiplicity control may inflate the chance of meeting the 70% threshold by chance.
The counter relationship may change across seasons due to rule changes, coaching trends, or personnel shifts, undermining a pooled league-wide test.

design.estimand: The within-unit average difference in points per possession (PPP) on PULL_UP possessions occurring after a PNR failure window (`lift`), compared to the unit's baseline PULL_UP PPP. A 'PNR failure' is defined as a game in which the offense's H1 PNR PPP falls below the 20th percentile of its own season distribution AND the team runs at least 5 PNR possessions in each half. Units are offensively-defined team-seasons. The primary metrics are: (i) the proportion of units with positive lift (`prop_pos`) and (ii) the median lift across units (`med_lift`).
design.unit: team-season (offensive unit), e.g., 2024-25 Boston Celtics offense
design.sample: All NBA teams from 2022-23 through 2025-26 regular seasons and playoffs, excluding garbage time (score margin >20 in Q4 or >15 in last 2 minutes), with a minimum of 20 qualifying PULL_UP possessions after PNR failure per unit (if no unit meets this, the test is not proceedable).
design.power: Power analysis must be conducted via simulation using historical data. Under optimistic assumptions (50 units, average 40 post-failure PULL_UP possessions, baseline lift SD 0.08, true median lift 0.02), power for a one-sided Wilcoxon test of median>0.02 is approximately 60-70%. For the binomial test of prop_pos>=0.70 against a null of 0.50, power with 50 units may be low (~50%). These figures need validation in a pilot, but the likely low power supports the do_not_proceed recommendation.
design.controls: Baseline PULL_UP PPP for each unit estimated from non-failure games in the same season via leave-one-out or pre-failure periods. Additional covariates: game score margin at start of possession, period, seconds remaining, opponent defensive rating, home/away, rest days, and a categorical initiator quality tier (top-3 usage player vs other).
design.falsification: Placebo test A: randomly permute the PNR failure labels within each team-season and recompute lift; the proportion of positive-lift units should not exceed the null expectation. Placebo test B: measure lift for CUT possessions (a high-efficiency play type not expected to be a direct counter) after PNR failure; it should not show the same pattern. Placebo test C: shift the failure window to random games and verify that lift vanishes.
design.multiplicity: For the proportion-of-positive-units test, use a pre-registered one-sided exact binomial test at alpha=0.05. For the median lift test, use a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test against the 2pp threshold. Both are primary and require pre-registration; no further multiplicity adjustment is needed if only these two tests are performed.
design.decision_rule: Proceed to claim support if and only if both null hypotheses are rejected: (1) H0: prop_pos <= 0.70 is rejected in favor of prop_pos > 0.70 at alpha=0.05, and (2) H0: med_lift <= 0.02 is rejected in favor of med_lift > 0.02 at alpha=0.05. If only one is rejected, the result is deemed inconclusive. If neither, the hypothesis is rejected.
design.data_version: NBA stats API play-by-play and derived play-type possession records (INITIATED [source]) for regular season and playoffs 2022-23 through 2025-26, with classification rules locked as of a pre-registration date.
